name: Rodtipnote
description: Pinch the handle between thumb and two fingers near the guard so the point answers every small wrist turn.

name: Rodbase Strike
description: Extend the lead arm in a straight line and drive the narrow point at the centre of the target.

name: Stitchhit
description: Slide the lead foot a half step forward as the arm extends, landing a short prick on the nearest opening.

name: Backward Thread
description: Snap the point back to the guard right after contact so the arm is never left reaching.

name: Resting Waxgrip
description: Tap the opposing weapon sideways with the flat of the free hand while the point stays on its line.

name: Awlstay
description: Rest the point low before the hip and watch the opponent's lead hand, ready to rise at any step.

name: Folded Rodtip
description: Stand side-on with the point raised toward the opponent's eye line so the body presents a thin target.

name: Rodtipwedge
description: Jab the point toward the opponent's eye line to make them flinch and open the guard.

name: Firm Hairpoint
description: Probe with short pokes along the opponent's sleeve line until a gap in the cover shows.

name: Reedhop
description: Slide the rear foot back a shoulder width after each poke so the opponent's counter falls short.

name: Raised Tinyquill
description: Lift the wrist sharply so the small guard of the blade turns an incoming cut away from the forearm.

name: Probe Blow
description: On the count of one, plant the front foot and stab once, then hold the arm still for the check.

name: Level Boltpoint
description: Turn the hip forward as the arm extends so the weight of the body rides behind the narrow point.

name: Square Slimshaft
description: Angle the blade flat so it slips between two ribs of the target instead of striking bone.

name: Fixing Darn
description: Jab the point into the muscle of the opponent's forearm so the weapon hand loosens its grip.

name: Darnamble
description: Tap the lead foot twice on the ground to shift the weight, then step off line from the opponent's reach.

name: Lowered Spikeguard
description: Sweep the free forearm across the chest to brush a thrust past the body while the blade stays ready.

name: Snug Triprism
description: Hold the point at throat height without moving, so a wary opponent hesitates to close the distance.

name: Awlgauge
description: Roll the wrist through slow circles with the point drawing a small ring, loosening the joint before work.

name: Short Pin
description: Draw a small ring with the point and finish by driving it straight through the centre of the ring.

name: Firm Rodbase
description: Turn the wrist inward and prick the soft inside of the opponent's wrist as it passes.

name: Fixing Slimshaft
description: Show two quick half-thrusts at different heights, then drive the third at the side the opponent guarded less.

name: Pin Dodge
description: Slip the front foot diagonally outward while the blade keeps tracking the opponent's centre line.

name: Reedlid
description: Raise the thumb side of the grip and forearm to take a strike on the bone behind the wrist.

name: Rodtipcount
description: Hook one finger over the small guard to lock the hand against slipping when a thrust lands hard.

name: Ready Triprism
description: Turn the blade point-down along the forearm so the wrist and arm can take a cut.

name: Rodtipstrike
description: From the reverse hold, drop the elbow and drive the point downward into an opponent who is crouched or bent.

name: Rodtipdash
description: Roll the blade over the fingers from reverse to forward grip and lunge straight into the next thrust.

name: Smooth Needlerod
description: Roll the handle across the palm to change grips mid-step without lifting the point from the target line.

name: Hairpoint Drop
description: Close to chest range and drive the point upward under the ribs in a short, hidden motion.

name: Pushing Boltpoint
description: Twist the whole arm outward to break an opponent's hold on the wrist and free the blade.

name: Shifting Spikeguard
description: Pivot on the lead heel and withdraw behind the free shoulder so the grip stays covered while backing off.

name: Kind Rodtip
description: Breathe out slowly while sending a thin thread of qi down the blade to harden the point.

name: Sudden Seam
description: Thrust with a thread of qi in the point so it pierces cloth and leather that would turn a plain blade.

name: Swaying Stitch
description: Draw breath as the arm retracts, then settle the weight low for the next thrust.

name: Awlcowl
description: Brush qi over the flat of the blade to nudge an incoming edge off line without a hard collision.

name: Reedblow
description: Land three pricks on one target in a fixed pulse count, each carried by a fresh puff of qi.

name: Mild Tinyquill
description: Spread qi lightly down the sword arm to read the opponent's incoming step as a faint tingle.

name: Swaying Darn
description: Release the rear knee and step wide to the side, keeping the point trained on the opponent's centre.

name: Skipping Stitch
description: Advance along a single narrow line in short gliding steps so the body never widens its profile.

name: Light Thread
description: Step diagonally across the opponent's line to block a retreat, the point trailing at hip height.

name: Probe Strike
description: Push off the rear heel with a pulse of qi to extend the lunge a forearm past its normal reach.

name: Stitchdash
description: Circle in a crescent around the weapon side and prick the exposed flank before the opponent turns.

name: Holding Waxgrip
description: Hold a low, retreating guard with the point forward so every backward step is covered by the blade.

name: Rodtipreview
description: Tap the toe on the ground once to feel the footing, noting slick or uneven patches before committing.

name: Needlerod Count
description: Drag the point lightly along an opponent's cover to feel for the join where armour or cloth meets.

name: Narrow Darn
description: Slip the point into a strap gap or armour join found by dragging, then press home with a little qi.

name: Forward Rodtip
description: Flick the point under a belt or buckle strap and snap upward to part it.

name: Snug Needlerod
description: Turn the shoulder to hide your own gaps from the probing point and send the strike onto armour.

name: Stitchpause
description: Stride in close and press the opponent's blade arm against their body so it cannot draw back.

name: Waxgrip Note
description: Close the fist around the handle with the blade emerging below the little finger like an awl.

name: Descending Probe
description: Thrust from the closed fist so the opponent sees only a punch before the point lands.

name: Tinyquill Hit
description: Draw the stiletto from the sleeve with a forward flick and prick the nearest hand in the same motion.

name: Slimshaft Cowl
description: Raise the closed fist and forearm into a bar that stops a descending strike with the blade tucked away.

name: Pushing Hairpoint
description: Twist the awl hand outward against a grasp to slip the hold and re-aim the point.

name: Stitchdrop
description: Press qi into the awl fist and bore the point slowly through a quilted jerkin.

name: Backward Seam
description: Step back while sliding the blade into the sleeve, ending the exchange with nothing visible in hand.

name: Nabbing Stitch
description: Show the empty open palm as bait and let the opponent's eyes follow it while the other hand readies the point.

name: Smooth Rodbase
description: Gather qi into one small bead at the point of the blade before the thrust is released.

name: Low Thread
description: Release the gathered bead as the point lands so the pierce runs deeper than the arm's own weight allows.

name: Even Triprism
description: Pick one dot on the opponent's clothing and hold it in mind so each thrust lands on the same spot.

name: Threaddash
description: Repeat quick pricks into the chosen dot until the cloth or hide gives way.

name: Reedwedge
description: Thin the gathered qi over the forearm like a sheet to take a glancing blow on the arm bone.

name: Sideways Spikeguard
description: Retreat a pace while keeping the qi bead alive in the point so the next thrust starts fully charged.
